title: Counting: value_counts and unique
summary: For text columns the question is usually “how many of each?”. value_counts() counts each value, most common first. unique() lists the different values and nunique() says how many there are. Together they answer “who won most?” and “how many venues?” in a line.
objectives: Count how often each value appears with value_counts().
List the different values with unique(), and count them with nunique().
Read one count out of value_counts() by its label.
Turn counts into shares with normalize=True.

slides.h: By the end: the league table in one line
slides.say: matches.csv has one row per match and a Winner column. Counting the wins per team is the league table, and it’s one line.
points: The result is a Series: the labels are the teams, the values the counts.
p: matches.csv has one row per match and a Winner column. Counting the wins per team is the league table, and it’s one line.
The result is a Series: the labels are the teams, the values the counts.

import pandas as pd
m = pd.read_csv("matches.csv")
wins = m["Winner"].value_counts()
